clinical.citation: Levy et al. 2017 - Molecular and clinical delineation of 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome (PMID: 28573701)

variants.description: Heterozygous de novo 427 kb deletion at 2p16.1 (chr2:60624940-61051867) encompassing BCL11A and PAPOLG

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo 427 kb deletion that includes BCL11A and PAPOLG. The phenotype is attributed to the contiguous genes in the deletion, not to PAPOLG alone.
clinical.center_country: France (Hôpital Robert Debré / Cochin / APHP, Paris)

clinical.citation: ASHG 2015 - Molecular and clinical delineation of the 2p15-16.1 microdeletion syndrome (Levy J, et al.)

variants.description: Heterozygous de novo 427 kb deletion at 2p16.1 (chr2:60624940-61051867) containing BCL11A and PAPOLG

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo deletion detected by SNP-array that includes BCL11A and PAPOLG. It is not specific to PAPOLG.

biological.citation: 2025 - SARS-CoV-2-Induced PAPOLG Contributes to Inflammation Response by Stabilizing NF-κB mRNA (PMID: 40607946)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was upregulated in SARS-CoV-2-infected THP-1 macrophages. Knockdown promoted NF-κB mRNA degradation and lowered TNF-α and IL-6. Overexpression stabilized NF-κB mRNA and raised TNF-α and IL-6. Genes subject to alternative polyadenylation were enriched in immune pathways.

biological.citation: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation (PMID: 42594865)
biological.summary: The viral element Pt1 from Potamipivirus directly recruits canonical poly(A) polymerases (PAPγ/PAPOLG and PAPα) to drive cytoplasmic polyadenylation and stabilize linear mRNA. This extends PAPγ function beyond nuclear, transcription-coupled pre-mRNA processing.

biological.citation: Systematic analysis of the frequently amplified 2p15-p16.1 locus reveals PAPOLG as a potential proto-oncogene in follicular and transformed follicular lymphoma (PMID: 31410080)
biological.summary: 2p15-p16.1 amplification is associated with increased PAPOLG and BCL11A transcription in tFL. PAPOLG expression rose further after histological transformation and was significantly overexpressed in FL compared with normal B-cells. PAPOLG is proposed as a potential proto-oncogene.
biological.significance: significant overexpression vs normal B-cells (p-value not given in abstract)

biological.citation: Comprehensive analysis of GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG axis in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 35482720)
biological.summary: PAPOLG is highly expressed in HCC and associated with poor prognosis. It is part of a predicted ceRNA axis (GSEC/miR-101-3p/SNX16/PAPOLG) linked to prognosis and to macrophage polarization/immune infiltration.
biological.significance: Risk model AUC 0.691, 0.623 and 0.626 at 1, 3 and 5 years

biological.citation: Traka et al. 2013 - A diet rich in high-glucoraphanin broccoli interacts with genotype to reduce discordance in plasma metabolite profiles by modulating mitochondrial function (PMID: 23964055)
biological.summary: SNPs in PAPOLG separated two metabolic phenotypes in the high-glucoraphanin broccoli arm. PAPOLG genotype and genotype × diet had significant effects on the plasma metabolome (lipids, amino acids, TCA intermediates, acylcarnitines). The diet reduced differences between genotypes, consistent with a role in mitochondrial function.
biological.significance: PAPOLG genotype P<0.001; genotype × diet P<0.001

biological.citation: A combined blood based gene expression and plasma protein abundance signature for diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer - OVCAD consortium (PMID: 23551967)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was one of 13 leukocyte genes whose blood expression differed in epithelial ovarian cancer patients. Combined with plasma proteins, the signature discriminated EOC from controls.
biological.sample_size: 343 samples for the 13-gene panel; 224 EOC patients and 65 controls for the combined model

biological.citation: Oocyte quality and in vivo embryo survival after ovarian stimulation in nulliparous and multiparous rabbit does (PMID: 35724452)
biological.summary: PAPOL-G (and PAPOL-A, MATER, ZAR1) expression in rabbit oocytes differed among superovulation and parity groups. This links poly(A) polymerase gamma expression to oocyte competence and the oocyte-embryo transition.
biological.significance: Differences among groups reported (p-value not given in abstract)

biological.citation: Analysis of differentially expressed microRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells treated with lipoteichoic acid (PMID: 35997417)
biological.summary: PAPOLG was among the differentially expressed predicted targets of LTA-responsive miRNAs in bovine mammary epithelial cells. These targets were enriched in MAPK signalling and related pathways.

PAPOLG lies within a 1.11 Mb 2p15-p16.1 deletion in a child with developmental delay, microcephaly and dysmorphism. It lies outside the narrowed critical region (KIAA1841, C2orf74, AHSA2, USP34), so it is not a leading candidate.
